name: Conduction
description: Heat flow between two thermal bodies: the target's temperature changes at Conductance × (source temperature − target temperature) / Thermal capacitance. Connect it between two Thermal masses, a Battery or a Temperature boundary (it reads and changes their Temperature). Conductance (W/K, default 50) is how readily heat moves for each kelvin of difference. Thermal capacitance (J/K, default 1000) is how much heat the target needs to warm by one kelvin; use the target's own value. The edge is bidirectional: the same temperature change is applied to the source with its sign flipped, so the source cools by exactly as many kelvin as the target warms. That conserves energy exactly only when both bodies have the same thermal capacitance, because the source's change is worked out with the target's. For two bodies of different size use Thermal link, and to hold a Temperature boundary fixed use One-way conduction; both give the right heat flow in those cases.
